newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says not targetting Australian dlr.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says not targetting Australian dlr.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said the government was not targetting a particular value for the Australian dollar.
"We're not targetting a particular value of the dollar," Costello said when asked if the rate cut announced by the Reserve Bank of Australia was having the desired effect on the Australian dollar.
"But as the Reserve said in its statement today, over a period of time, the dollar has risen," Costello told reporters.
"One of the consequences of that is that it's kept pressure on prices and that has made a contribution to lower inflation."
The RBA said earlier it would reduce official interest rates to 6.0 percent from 6.5 percent, a move which surprised financial markets as rates were last cut only on November 6, by the same amount.
In its statement announcing the cut, the central bank said the reduction essentially reflected a further improvement in the inflationary outlook.
"This improvement in the inflation outlook is influenced by the strength of the exchange rate which, despite the volatility of last week, remains above its average of recent months," the RBA said.
The Australian dollar reached a six year high above 82 U.S. cents early last week, driven up by international investors chasing high yields.
It slumped in response to the latest monetary policy easing by the RBA, tumbling to 79.62 cents, although dealers said at this level it represented a good buying opportunity.
